notes: Bar-Adon, HA 40: a cave above 'Ein el-Ghuweir; in the region by description (reader place ein_ghuweir), no point of its own, so not in the 50 m test. INFERENCE: probably the cave the lane holds as A41:XIV/51 ('above the 'Ein el-Ghuweir site'); no source states the identity, so it is not merged.

Patrich, ESI 2 pp. 65-66 ('Mar Saba Map') summarises the survey the lane holds as ASI Map 109/7. The coding names the grotto of St. Saba; the lane holds two caves under Sabas's name (Great Laura Complex 37 'Cave of St Sabas'; 109/7 site 63 'Cave of Sabas'). Either way the cave is already a lane row, so the IAA row is not added. The coding gives no clause value.
Nahal 'Arugot seal impression report: a cave with sherds; no opening or facing in the coding.

Goldfuss, ESI 3 pp. 106-107: laura complex of natural and man-made caves; plural with no count, so a cluster row (PLAN 4.1(4)). Its point coincides with the nine caves A41:II/33-41 (flagged by the 50 m rule).

Same report: two plastered burial caves (cluster of 2). The quote describes one cave's entrance on the slope; a statement about one member does not cover the cluster (PLAN 4.1(4)), so no clause value.

Hirschfeld, ESI 7-8 pp. 95-97: a large natural cave used for domestic purposes and a cave church (n_features 2, cluster of 2). INFERENCE: the monastery founded in 411 CE, 218 m from ASI 109/4 site 108 (Deir Mukallik Cave); no name is stated, so not flagged.
Eshel, ESI 7-8 'Makkuk Cave' (coded p. c. 116; the lane cites p. 117): the report the lane coded under S5. Not added.
'Cave of the Pool', Nahal David: a lane proper name (Zissu; ASI 147 site 149). Not added. The coding speaks of 'the entrance' in the singular, as ASI 147-149 already has n_openings 1: no change.
'En Gedi burial cave hewn in the cliff; the subtype gives one entrance (0.7 x 0.8 m) with a sealing stone and no other opening. 143 m from ASI 147-272 (not flagged).
'Cave of the Pool', Nahal David (another season). Not added; no clause value in the coding.
'Cave of the Rope (No. 347B)', Nahal 'Arugot, natural cliff cave. The lane holds no cave of this name or number; nearest lane point ASI 147-128 at 60 m (not flagged).
Nahal Hever Cave B: 'two entrances (east and west)'. Neither member is northern, so C5 stays unknown (A6 cannot fail a pair). 36 m from ASI 147-413 (flagged by the 50 m rule).
Hever Nostrils Cave (C1-001): 'three entrances'. Roman, no closer dating.
Nahal Hazazon: a small cave with a wide mouth at the foot of a cliff. The coding's retaining wall is not placed in front of the mouth, so the terrace clause stays unknown (AMENDMENT_1 item 3).
'Cave of the Pool', Nahal David (another season). Not added; 'entrance area' in the singular, as ASI 147-149: no change.

Patrich and Arubas, ESI 13 p. 61, Wadi Murrar 'Ein Abu Mahmud caves (four caves, 6th-7th c.). The lane's WBADB row E519 has the same name, a point 1 m away, and cites Patrich and Arubas: identity stated by that citation. Not added.

Peleg, HA-ESI 112 p. 73*, Mishor Adummim: WBADB E572 cites this excavation. Not added. The coding gives one opening, facing south ('natural cave, opening facing south, walled'). Applied to E572 it would make C3 fail (one opening) and C4 fail (south) at the cave level; E572 is now unknown on both branches and would become fail. Reported, not applied.
